name: Hawthorn extract for chronic heart failure
summary: Across the placebo-controlled trials pooled in a Cochrane review, hawthorn extract added to conventional treatment improved physiologic exercise capacity (maximal workload, exercise tolerance) and heart-failure symptoms, and lowered the pressure–heart rate product.
description: Guo, Pittler & Ernst (Cochrane 2008, CD005312) reviewed double-blind, placebo-controlled RCTs of hawthorn extract as an adjunct in chronic heart failure. Ten trials provided data suitable for meta-analysis of physiologic and symptom outcomes; per-arm means and SDs are taken from the review's forest plots.
interpretation: Benefits were seen on physiologic surrogates (maximal workload WMD ~5 W, exercise tolerance, pressure–heart rate product) and on symptom scores. Most trials were small, short, and predate modern guideline-directed heart-failure therapy, and no trial was powered for mortality or hospitalization, so these are surrogate endpoints rather than hard outcomes.
methodologyNotes: Per-arm mean/SD/n for each outcome are transcribed from the Cochrane review's forest plots (Analyses 1.1–1.6); the engine recomputes each mean difference and the random-effects pool. Continuous outcomes are pooled as mean differences (same units within each outcome). Tauchert 2002 contributes a high-dose (HD) and a low-dose (LD) arm that share one placebo group, exactly as entered in the review. For the 6-minute walk test the review tabled the arms in control–treatment order (reported MD −8); entered here with the hawthorn and placebo arm values in their own columns, so the engine's mean difference carries the opposite sign for the same magnitude.

outcomes.label: Pressure–heart rate product
outcomes.description: Systolic blood pressure × heart rate, an index of myocardial oxygen consumption; a decrease is beneficial.

outcomes.label: Symptom score (von Zerssen)
outcomes.description: Self-rated complaint score (von Zerssen); a decrease reflects symptom improvement.
